question: When three different numbers from the set \(\{ -3, -2, -1, 4, 5 \}\) are multiplied, the largest possible product is
solution:
A positive product is possible, so any negative product can be ruled out. There are only two positive numbers available, so a positive product of three different numbers must use two negatives and one positive. Choosing one or three negatives would give a negative product.

The possible products of two different negative numbers are
\[
(-3)(-2)=6,\qquad (-3)(-1)=3,\qquad (-2)(-1)=2.
\]
The largest is \(6\). Since these pair products are positive, using \(5\) as the third factor gives a larger result than using \(4\). Therefore the largest possible product is
\[
(-3)(-2)(5)=6\cdot5=30,
\]
which is choice C.
